angle: DL/EDGE: Run-the-Hoop Hoop G (the hardest sideways push held for half a second around the hoop, year-standardized) vs NFL pressure rate, read as a change-of-direction force marker rather than bend; baseline = log pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS athleticism + games per season + official 10-yd split and 3-cone (imputed with a flag; observed-only tests reported)
metric_name: Hoop G: peak half-second sideways (path-perpendicular) acceleration in the Run-the-Hoop drill, g, z within Combine year, corrected for one-run reliability 0.41
headline_number: 0.6 extra pressures per 450-rush season per sd, 90% [-0.4, 1.7] (n=90, skeptical prior; 2x 1.5 [0.0, 3.1], wide 2.0 [0.1, 4.0]). Out of class, fully nested (screen, prior scale and reliability re-chosen inside each training fold): held-out log score +0.58 +/- 0.49 (positive in 3 of 3 classes; Hoop G chosen in 2 of 3 folds; wide prior -0.18 +/- 1.39); R2 change least squares -0.026 [-0.286, 0.185], ridge 0.056 [-0.200, 0.155] (n=63); Hoop G fixed in advance +0.088, positive in 3 of 3 (optimistic).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_06 winner (revised), applying the four judges' top_changes. Data science: the not-fully-nested +1.36 log score is replaced by a fully nested one (14-pair screen, chosen drill, its reliability and the prior scale all set on the two training classes; per-class values and the fold-selected drill reported: +0.58 +/- 0.49); prior sensitivity moved into the main table next to the out-of-class tests; posterior-predictive check (80% intervals cover 88%, spread p=0.75); cross-fitted per-class estimates are now Fig 3; a fully nested ridge alternative on the 63 plus a fixed-feature least-squares bound; numbers.json trimmed to exactly the keys the text uses with no *_abs duplicates, plus claims.json (key -> sentence); writeup/check.py now accepts the magnitude of signed values and, when claims.json exists, flags orphan keys. Football: Fig 1 rebuilt as trace validation for Robinson, Ezeiruaku, Tuipulotu and Phillips (hoop path + sideways-g trace next to his hardest-turning NFL rush and its g trace, 2-yd scale bars); 'bend' dropped from every board column and label; rule table split EDGE vs interior (plus / minus / film-first / one-run retest / no call); pressure rate vs forecast in every board row; concrete draft-room example (Sawyer 123 vs Sorrell 124: 0.7 pressures, about pick 124 -> 94); 2023-24 plus calls named as hits or misses; one-line comparison with the 3-cone (partial rho 0.41, n=27) and 10-yd split (0.11, n=54); pre-reg power 0.12 stated as a reason for low stakes; appendix cut; pair statistics cut to one sentence. Writeup: shorter plain title; two-sentence lede of about 60 words; top table cut to 3 rows; 'Why' rewritten as three beats; coach-repeatable definition; jargon glossed (beta-binomial explained, nats replaced by 'x times as likely', Laplace/R-hat removed). Viz: Fig 1 text 12-15 pt, no orange, scale bars, nothing clipped, 79-DL scatter removed (its rho stays in Fig 2 and the caption); Fig 3 is one forest in one unit (pressures per season) on the 90 with the nested log score per fold beside each class; Fig 4 is a player-card board with a hoop sparkline on every row, a distinct film-first diamond with legend entry, and hits/misses in the title; Fig 2 x-range trimmed to 0.85 and a single-claim title. 1,776 words, 4 figures + 3 tables; check.py passes.
open_risks: The fully nested log score is positive under the skeptical and 2x priors but negative under the wide prior; judges may still read the out-of-class evidence as prior-driven.
Ridge (+0.056) and least-squares (-0.026) nested R2 disagree in sign, and both intervals span zero; the fixed-feature +0.088 is optimistic because Hoop G was chosen after seeing all three classes.
The 3-cone shows a larger partial rho than Hoop G (0.41 vs 0.32) on only 27 players; the 'Hoop G covers rushers who skipped the 3-cone' use case rests on that small comparison.
Trace validation uses each rusher's hardest-turning of 20 sampled random snaps (a maximum, so biased upward) and no film; the mechanism remains unknown.
The film-first flags are defined from NFL outcomes, so they apply only to players already in the league, not to draft prospects.
